title: Decentralized signatory ledger for timeboxed model transitions (RBAC + audit)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a robust, auditable mechanism for promoting model versions across staged environments without central approval bottlenecks. Current gating relies on manual signoffs and ad-hoc Slack approvals which causes delays and poor traceability. This ticket scopes a decentralized signatory ledger: a timeboxed, event-sourced ledger that records entitlements, signatories, evidence bundles, and automatic expiry/escalation rules. Ledger entries are immutable, linked to RBAC roles, and surfaced in the Console to satisfy audit and compliance requirements.
proposal_summary: Implement an event-sourced promotion ledger service backed by our audit store. Key features: (1) RBAC-to-entitlement mapping (teams can delegate promotion rights for specific model namespaces); (2) timeboxed entitlements with TTLs and auto-expiry; (3) evidence bundles attached to each approval (links to evals, dashboards, PRs); (4) automatic escalation rules when required sign-offs are missing or thresholds exceeded; (5) signed ledger entries (HMAC) to ensure tamper-evidence; (6) UI for reviewers and programmatic API for automation/pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger service stores immutable promotion events with timestamp, actor, role, model-version, and evidence links
RBAC enforcement: only principals with matching entitlements can create 'approve' events for a model namespace
Timeboxed entitlements expire automatically and are visible in Console; expired approvals cannot be used to promote
Evidence bundle support: each approval can reference or upload a compressed evidence payload (eval ids, dashboards, PR link)
Audit view in Console surfaces a chain of approvals and can export a forensic bundle for compliance
Auto-escalation: if required signoffs missing after TTL, system notifies escalation owners and marks promotion as blocked
Integration tests cover API, RBAC checks, expiry behavior, and ledger immutability assertions
tradeoffs: Event-sourced ledger increases storage and indexing cost vs a lightweight approval table, but yields better forensic traceability
Strong RBAC checks add friction for small teams; we will provide temporary scoped entitlements to reduce friction
HMAC-signed entries are sufficient for tamper evidence internally; integrating a public append-only log (e.g., consortium ledger) is out of scope for MVP
Evidence bundles increase payload size — we will store large artifacts in object storage and reference them from the ledger
decisions: Use existing audit-store (Elasticsearch-backed) for indexing ledger events instead of building new DB
Represent entitlements as first-class objects linked to existing org/team RBAC mappings
MVP will support policy-based TTLs and single-level escalation; multi-tier escalation deferred
Signed ledger entries will use project KMS-derived HMAC keys, not full asymmetric signatures for MVP
rollout_plan: Design & spec (Mar 1 - Mar 7): finalize schema, RBAC mappings, Console UX for signatory list
Prototype API (Mar 8 - Mar 14): implement create/read/list ledger endpoints, unit tests
Security review & pilot (Mar 15 - Mar 21): run threat model, pilot with two internal teams and Runtime canary
Iterate & pilot expansion (Mar 22 - Mar 28): incorporate pilot feedback, add auto-escalation notifications
GA rollout (Apr 1): enable for all orgs with opt-out via org policy
qa_and_test_plan: Unit tests for RBAC mapping and entitlement checks
Integration tests simulating parallel approvals, expiry, and auto-escalation
Fuzz tests for evidence bundle attachments and storage
Manual compliance verification: export forensic bundle and validate schema against compliance checklist
Load test: simulate 1000 promotion events/day per region to validate indexing and Console performance
